acceptance: A terminal tab is titled by its folder's name: the last path segment, ignoring a trailing separator, for POSIX and Windows paths alike; the root keeps its slash and an empty path reads as an em dash.

Input and resizes reach a session in the order they were made; a paste over 1 MiB is refused with a visible message before anything is sent; input a session can no longer take fails visibly instead of being kept to replay later.

reason: TS queues resize messages to its PTY process and coalesces consecutive ones. The native session applies each resize to its PTY in process, in the order asked, behind the same bounded request queue as input, so there is no message backlog to coalesce.

acceptance: Output waits in a bounded queue for the session's screen: a noisy process whose screen does not read stops at its writes instead of filling memory, and finishes once its screen reads again; closing a session ends a process even while its output waits unread. The session's own screen is the one responder to terminal queries: a cursor position report is answered exactly once, also when the query arrives split.

reason: TS streams PTY output to a renderer display in frames acknowledged one at a time, and can recreate a crashed display from a replay buffer without respawning. The native screen (the vt100 parser) lives in the same process as its session for the session's whole life, reading output as it arrives; there is no separate display to acknowledge frames or to recreate.

acceptance: Sessions started together, in one folder or several, each run in the folder they were given at their own size, sharing no request state; each carries the presentation colors it was started with.

OSC 10/11 default-color probes are answered with the current theme's colors and removed from what the screen shows, also when a probe is split across output chunks; later probes get the theme as it is then.

reason: TS receives renderer colors as untyped numbers and keeps xterm's own path when one is out of range. Native colors come from the theme as 8-bit channels by type, so no invalid color can reach the responder.

TS serializes an xterm screen and restores a checkpoint of its modes (scroll regions, tab stops, saved cursor, charsets, alternate screen) when a display is recreated, and must not checkpoint inside an escape or surrogate pair. The native screen is never serialized: hiding, resizing, moving tabs and switching projects keep the same parser instance, so there is no checkpoint to continue from.

acceptance: What leaves an Agent's Hook names files, never their content: a patch names the files it touches (update, add, delete) without its body; a write keeps only its path; Cursor's conversation is the session; Codex 0.147.0's own Bash and apply_patch payloads keep only file names, never the shell command or patch body. Literal reads in pipelines, quoted names and sed scripts name their files; anything that depends on shell state (variables, globs, substitutions, a changed directory, in-place edits, other programs) names none. Each provider's own start event and tool name begin that kind of activity on the named file, a projected shell read is a read of exactly those files, an unsupported shell command has no target, and Cursor ending its session while the shell stays open ends only that source session. A plain shell is instrumented for every enrolled Agent, without naming one provider.

An Agent CLI's terminal is active while its title shows a spinner frame or a busy status (Working, Running shell command, Planning) and not for Ready, Waiting or a plain title; every Agent gets the same output pulse, active until the output idle interval after its last output; an explicit busy title stays active through silence until it says Ready; a host-owned presentation refresh hides only its own repaint, never what the title says; a plain shell never reports activity.
A tab still choosing its launcher closes at once; a terminal asks before closing while it starts or runs, and closes unasked once it exited or failed.

reason: TS keeps a terminal-only tab-group reducer (desktopTerminalSessionsReducer) that only its split visual smoke harness uses; the product's terminal tabs are Workbench items, and their groups, splits, moves, merges and failed launches are the Workbench's, mapped with the workbench tests. Native terminals have only the Workbench model, where a group emptied by a move stays until closed rather than collapsing.
